raw_case_text: A 55-year-old, widowed, postmenopausal, parous (G6, P6, L6, A0), diabetic female, belonging to low socioeconomic strata presented with gradually enlarging painful swelling over genitalia for 3 years. The patient complained of difficulty in walking due to the mass. There was a history of cutaneous TB over the left cheek 6 years back. The patient was started on anti-tubercular treatment (ATT) for the same. However, she discontinued the treatment within a few months by herself after she noticed orange discoloration of urine. There was no recent history of cough, weight loss, or loss of appetite. There was no history of exposure to the risk of sexually transmitted disease. On examination, a single, well-defined, hard, tender pedunculated swelling, approximately 25 cm x 20 cm [Figures 1A and 2A] and an oval, nonpedunculated swelling measuring 20 cm x 12 cm in size [Figures 1B and 2B] was present over left and right labia majora, respectively, with overlying nodular-peau de'orange like surface along with a single well defined hypopigmented patch and centrally hyperpigmented macules over the medial aspect of right labial swelling. Fissuring along with maceration was present along bilateral inguinal folds. There was a similar swelling present peri-anally measuring 4.5 cm x 3.5 cm [Figure 2C] with surrounding hyperpigmented skin. There was no associated inguinal lymphadenopathy. Per-abdominal, per-vaginal, and per-rectal examination were unremarkable. Based on clinical appearance, vulval TB, leiomyoma, fibroma, malignancy, vulval elephantiasis, and lymphogranuloma venereum were kept as differentials. Elicitation of history and previous documentation revealed that the patient had been treated with oral Doxycycline 100 mg twice a day for 21 days prior to admission to a tertiary healthcare facility. Chest radiographs and routine blood investigations were normal. Mantoux test was inconclusive. The HIV antibody test was nonreactive. The possibility of elephantiasis secondary to filariasis was ruled out by a blood smear examination for microfilariae. Ultrasonography was suggestive of a lobulated heterogeneous solid mass with internal vascularity and thickening of the labial wall. The dermatology quality life index was 15, suggesting a very large effect of the lesion on the patient's life. As the mass was huge, the patient was referred to general surgery, where complete excision of the vulval and peri-anal mass, along with reconstructive surgery, was done, and specimens were sent for histopathological examination. Microscopy revealed multiple tuberculous granulomas and fibrosis, which with central were suggestive of chronic inflammation. Granulomas caseating necrosis surrounded by Epitheloid cells, Langhan's type giant cells, lymphocytes, and plasma cells were seen [Figures 3 and 4]. Periodic acid schiff and Acid-Fast Bacillus (AFB) stains were negative. The patient was then started on ATT. The surgical site healed with minimal scarring without any undue complications, and there was a drastic improvement in the quality of life of the patient during the course of treatment [Figure 5].

subjective.chief_complaint: A 55-year-old diabetic female presenting with a 3-year history of gradually enlarging, painful vulval and perianal masses causing difficulty walking.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with a 3-year history of progressively enlarging, painful bilateral labial and perianal swellings that impaired ambulation (Dermatology Life Quality Index score of 15). Prior to referral, she had received a 21-day course of oral doxycycline 100 mg twice daily without resolution.
subjective.past_medical_history: Widowed, postmenopausal, multiparous (G6P6L6A0) female with diabetes mellitus and a history of cutaneous tuberculosis of the left cheek 6 years earlier, for which she prematurely self-discontinued anti-tubercular therapy (ATT) after a few months due to rifampicin-induced orange urine discoloration. No history of STI exposure.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for painful genital swelling and gait difficulty; negative for cough, fever, weight loss, or anorexia.

objective.physical_examination: Genital examination revealed a well-defined, hard, tender pedunculated left labium majus mass (25 x 20 cm), an oval non-pedunculated right labium majus swelling (20 x 12 cm) with a nodular peau d'orange surface and hypopigmented/hyperpigmented macules, bilateral inguinal fold fissuring and maceration, and a 4.5 x 3.5 cm perianal swelling. No inguinal lymphadenopathy; abdominal, vaginal, and rectal exams were normal.
objective.routine_investigations: Routine blood tests and chest radiograph were normal. HIV antibody test was nonreactive, Mantoux test was inconclusive, and peripheral blood smear for microfilariae was negative. Local ultrasonography showed a lobulated heterogeneous solid mass with internal vascularity and labial wall thickening.
objective.advanced_workup: Histopathological examination of the excised vulval and perianal masses demonstrated caseating epithelioid granulomas with Langhans giant cells, lymphocytes, plasma cells, and fibrosis; PAS and tissue AFB stains were negative.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Vulval and perianal cutaneous tuberculosis (lupus vulgaris/hypertrophic vulval TB) presenting as pseudo-elephantiasis, confirmed by caseating granulomatous histopathology; lymphatic filariasis (negative microfilaria smear), HIV, and fungal infection were ruled out.
Plan & Outcome: Underwent complete surgical excision of the vulval and perianal masses with vulval reconstruction followed by standard anti-tubercular therapy (ATT), achieving complete wound healing with minimal scarring and marked improvement in quality of life.
